operation_type.description: Provide the operation type. Allowed values: Create, Modify. Synonyms must be normalized to the canonical value.
operation_type.x-a2at-value-constraint: Allowed canonical values: Create, Modify. Normalize synonyms to the canonical value instead of treating them as out-of-range: Add / Implement / Establish / Deploy / Set Up / Provision / New / Enable / Activate / Configure are all Create; Update / Adjust / Change / Revise / Edit are all Modify. When the input carries a power outage / fault-alarm background and asks to maintain or adjust the throughput / rate guarantee of the affected sites, the operation type is Modify, even when no explicit modify verb appears — do NOT leave it null or report it as missing in this case.

task_description.description: Dynamically provide the task description based on the operation type (Create/Modify).
examples: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), execute the energy-saving task to achieve the goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target), and return the wireless network energy saving result in the format defined in [Expected Output](#expected-output).
task_description.x-a2at-value-constraint: When the type is [Create]: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), execute the energy-saving task to achieve the goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target), and return the wireless network energy saving result in the format defined in [Expected Output](#expected-output). When the type is [Modify]: Based on [Task Object](#task-object) and [Task Context](#task-context), execute the energy-saving task to achieve the goal defined in [Task Target](#task-target). The value must always be non-null. Output the fixed text verbatim; there is no need to replace [Task Object](#task-object), [Task Context](#task-context), [Task Target](#task-target) or [Expected Output](#expected-output) with actual slot values — these are in-document anchor links, not placeholders.

task_object.description: Explicitly specify the energy saving coverage scope information, a geographic or logical area (e.g., district-level administrative unit). The area information is a required parameter.
task_object.x-a2at-value-constraint: Area name. A named region (a specific region name such as "RegionX" or "Slice A") is valid. Only anonymous vague descriptions that carry no concrete region name, such as "test area", "sites in this area", "all communities", "indoor communities", or "outdoor communities", must report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Area' and actual describing what is missing. Only one region name is allowed; if the input specifies multiple regions, report slot.constraint_violated.

task_target.description: Define the quantitative or qualitative goals the task must achieve. Quantitative and qualitative goals cannot be selected at the same time. Do not default to a qualitative goal — extract a goal only when the input expresses one.
task_target.x-a2at-value-constraint:
1. Quantitative goal: energy saving gain target as a single percentage (e.g. 15%). A range is NOT a single value — you MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Energy saving gain target'. Range formats include '20%-30%', '20% - 30%', '20% ~ 30%', '20% to 30%'.
2. Qualitative goal: maximize energy saving under the task context conditions. Use [terminology] only to RECOGNIZE whether the input phrase is a valid mode (Aggressive Energy Saving / Maximize Energy Saving; Conservative Energy Saving / Maximize User Experience Assurance / Maximize KPI Assurance; GS) — do NOT convert or rewrite the phrase: keep the input's original wording verbatim in the Task Target. A GS-related phrase (e.g. 'apply high GS', 'high GS', 'set GS to 5', 'GS 5') IS a valid qualitative energy-saving aggressiveness goal. A phrase that matches none of the valid modes or their synonyms (e.g. 'green', 'eco', 'balanced', 'auto') reports slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Energy saving mode'. A numeric throughput/rate/UX target is a rate guarantee goal, not a mode, and must not be treated as a mode violation. A phrase like 'maximize the rate', 'maximize the rate as much as possible', 'maximizing the rate as much as possible', 'as large a rate as possible' or 'the highest possible rate' is a vague rate guarantee goal, NOT an energy saving mode — do NOT report it as a mode violation.

task_context.description: Provide the background and context information for task execution.
examples: Cell RAT for energy saving: NR; Energy saving time range: start time "08:00:00", end time "12:00:00"; Rate guarantee target: {00:00-06:00, 2Mbps}, {06:00-18:00, 10Mbps}.
task_context.x-a2at-value-constraint:
Apply these rules in order. Each rule gives the trigger condition and the error to report. You MUST report the error when the trigger is met; do NOT silently fix, normalize, or extract the value as valid. Terminology handling: the [terminology] section is for understanding the input only. Do NOT normalize terms from the input into their canonical terminology-table forms when building the Task Context — carry the input's original wording (synonyms such as 'User Experience First', 'maximize energy saving', '5G', '1080p') into the Task Context verbatim; never drop or rewrite such a phrase. When a terminology phrase does not fit another field, append it to the Task Context as its own line. The example in this slot's schema illustrates the output FORMAT only — output a field only when the input states it; do not fill in fields just because they appear in the example.
1. Cell RAT: the default is NO Cell RAT — omit 'Cell RAT for energy saving' from the output unless the input explicitly states a RAT. NEVER derive the Cell RAT from a site or cell name: such names may contain the letters LTE, NR or LNR, but those embedded letters are part of the name and do NOT state a Cell RAT. Extract the RAT only when a RAT term appears as its own word in the input, outside any name. When the input does state a Cell RAT: only LTE, NR, LNR, all are valid (synonyms in [terminology] below). When the input uses a synonym (e.g. 'E-UTRAN', '4G', 'NG-RAN', '5G'), keep the input's original wording verbatim in the output — do NOT rewrite it to the canonical LTE/NR. Always use the label 'Cell RAT for energy saving'. Phrases such as 'coverage restricted to E-UTRAN cell' or 'Energy-Saving Scope is NG-RAN' ARE explicit mentions of the Cell RAT — extract them (keeping the original wording). Invalid values such as '3G', '2G', 'WiFi' MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Cell RAT'. Do NOT rewrite an invalid RAT to a valid one (e.g. do NOT change '3G' to 'NR').
2. Cross-task reference: when the input mentions earlier/previous tasks, run this check before any other rule. Count the earlier tasks the input describes — an enumeration such as 'one covered ...; the other covered ...' counts as TWO — and apply this rule regardless of how the tasks or their regions are named or numbered. If the count is TWO or more and the new task reuses their parameters through a phrase like 'same as the previous task' WITHOUT saying which one to inherit from, the reference is ambiguous, even when one earlier task was mentioned last and looks like the obvious referent; NEVER resolve 'the previous task' to the last-mentioned task. You MUST set the task_context value to null and report {"slot_name": "task_context", "code": "slot.constraint_violated", "facts": {"slot_label": "Task reference", "actual": "same as the previous task"}}. Regions, RATs, time windows and rates appearing only inside the earlier-task descriptions are NOT values of the new task: do not extract them into any slot, and do not report them as multiple regions under 'Area'. Example — input: 'two earlier tasks: one in RegionX, NR, 00:00:00-06:00:00, 5 Mbps; the other in RegionY, same RAT and window, 2 Mbps. Create the next one: same as the previous task, but the area moves to RegionZ.' → correct extraction: operation_type="Create", task_object="RegionZ", task_context=null, slot_errors=[{"slot_name": "task_context", "code": "slot.constraint_violated", "facts": {"slot_label": "Task reference", "actual": "same as the previous task"}}] (extract the other slots normally).
3. Energy saving time range, recurring daily; if omitted, full-period energy saving. Rate goal is guaranteed only within this range. Its output format is fixed and MUST match the example verbatim: Energy saving time range: start time "HH:MM:SS", end time "HH:MM:SS" — always keep the seconds (e.g. 00:00:00, 22:00:00), always quote the clock values, and keep the exact label and separators; do NOT shorten it to '00:00-22:00' or 'from 00:00 to 22:00'. In a power outage scenario where the operation type is Modify, include the energy saving time range only when the input explicitly states it — do NOT derive it from the power outage window and do NOT default to a full period; when absent, omit 'Energy saving time range' from the output entirely.
4. Enable Lossless Experience Energy Saving: OPTIONAL — omit this field entirely when the input does not mention it; never invent, infer, or default it. When the input does mention it, you MUST extract it in one of these two forms: (a) if the input gives an explicit yes/no value, output 'Enable Lossless Experience Energy Saving: yes' or 'Enable Lossless Experience Energy Saving: no'; (b) if the input only uses a terminology phrase without an explicit yes/no (e.g. 'Lossless Experience Energy Saving', 'User Experience First', 'Lossy Experience Energy Saving', 'Energy Saving First'), keep that phrase verbatim as the value, either as the phrase alone on its own line. Do NOT convert the phrase to yes/no, do NOT rewrite it to another synonym or canonical form, and do NOT drop it. This rule only records the attribute; it must not create a rate guarantee target or change any other field.
5. Carrier frequencies that can be turned off. When the input mentions turning off / shutting down carrier frequencies (e.g. 'turn off the carrier frequencies', 'shut down carrier') but does NOT provide specific frequency numbers (e.g. 1600, 1650), you MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Carrier frequencies'. A frequency must be an exact number (e.g. 1600). Words like 'approximately', 'about', 'around', 'centered at approximately' before a frequency make it an approximation — you MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Carrier frequencies'. Do NOT remove the approximation word and extract the number as if it were exact.
6. Rate guarantee goal: minimum downlink throughput target and its effective time period. Area-level requires a time window and a rate; site-level requires site list, time-segmented rate goal, and optional background event and duration. When multiple sites carry different rate/time configurations, group them per site — Site list 1 / Site list 2 ... — each with its own site names, time-segmented rate goal and background event; do NOT flatten them into one merged description. Always normalize concrete numeric rate guarantee goals in the output: (1) an explicit time-segmented throughput / rate guarantee goal (e.g. 'set the guaranteed throughput as follows: 00:00-06:00 → 2Mbps', 'change the time-segmented rate guarantee goal to {08:00~11:00, 10Mbps}') MUST be formatted as '{HH:MM-HH:MM, rate}' (e.g. '{00:00-06:00, 2Mbps}'); a single/full-period goal inherits the energy saving time range as its window (e.g. energy saving range 00:00-22:00 with target 10 Mbps → 'Rate guarantee target: {00:00-22:00, 10Mbps}'); if no time range is stated, use {00:00-24:00, rate}. (2) A user-experience / video-quality / rate-terminology requirement phrased with specialized terms (e.g. 'ensuring user experience for 720p video', 'Set the User Experience Target to 5', 'Set the AVG DL THP to 5', 'Set the DL rate floor to 10') IS a rate guarantee target: keep the input's original wording verbatim as the rate content and wrap it in the same time-window format — 'Rate guarantee target: {HH:MM-HH:MM, <original phrase>}'. For a single/full-period target use the energy saving time range as the window: energy saving range 00:00-22:00 with 'Ensuring user experience for 720p video.' → 'Rate guarantee target: {00:00-22:00, Ensuring user experience for 720p video.}'. Do NOT convert the phrase to a numeric rate via the terminology table (e.g. do NOT turn '720p' into '2Mbps') and do NOT drop it. 'User experience first' / 'Energy saving first' are energy-saving modes, not rate targets — keep them as modes and do NOT create a rate guarantee target from them. (3) Historical or background throughput statements (e.g. 'The historical minimum downlink throughput was 2 Mbps') are context noise, NOT the target: never use a historical/background value as the target, never mix it into the target, and do NOT copy the historical/background statement into the Task Context. Rate goals WITHOUT a concrete value still report errors as above — do NOT normalize them.
Example of per-site grouping: for two sites with different rates, output as separate list items:
- Site list 1: ["Site A"], Time-segmented rate guarantee target: {08:00-13:00,10Mbps}, Background event: power outage from 08:00 to 18:00.
- Site list 2: ["Site B"], Time-segmented rate guarantee target: {13:00-18:00,1Mbps}, Background event: power outage from 08:00 to 18:00. Time windows MUST NOT overlap and must fall within the energy-saving execution period; overlapping windows report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Time windows'. Two windows overlap when one window's start time is earlier than the other window's end time, e.g. '10 Mbit/s from 08:00 to 12:00 and 5 Mbit/s from 10:00 to 18:00': the second window starts at 10:00, which is earlier than the first window's end 12:00, so the windows overlap (10:00-12:00 shared) and you MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Time windows'. Time period names such as 'idle period', 'regular period', 'busy period', 'peak period', 'off-peak period' are NOT explicit clock ranges — you MUST report slot.constraint_violated with slot_label 'Time windows'. A vague rate (e.g. 'maximize the rate', 'maximizing the rate as much as possible', 'as large a rate as possible', 'the highest possible rate' without a concrete number) MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Guaranteed rate' — never silently omit it. This applies even when the vague rate phrase appears as a subordinate clause of a request in a power outage scenario where the operation type is Modify. When the input says rate targets 'need to be adjusted' / 'need to change' / 'need to be modified' / uses an imperative like 'modify the guaranteed throughput target' and specifies a time range (e.g. 'adjusted from 08:00 to 12:00') but does NOT give a specific rate value (e.g. 10Mbps), you MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Guaranteed rate'. The presence of a time range without a rate value is the trigger. The time range may be stated explicitly (e.g. 'from 08:00 to 12:00') OR referenced indirectly (e.g. 'during the power outage', 'during the energy saving period' — these refer back to a previously stated time range and count as a time range). A general 'modify the throughput target' request with neither an explicit nor an indirect time range nor a rate value is acceptable.
7. In a power outage scenario where the operation type is Modify, the affected site list and power outage time are REQUIRED. (a) Site list: must be concrete site names. A site list is VALID if it contains one or more concrete site names. A single concrete site name (e.g. 'Modify the plan for SITE_A in RegionX') is a complete site list and MUST NOT be reported as not provided. To find the site list, look at what the plan is being modified FOR: in 'Modify the energy-saving plan for <name(s)> in <Area>', the name(s) between 'for' and 'in <Area>' ARE the affected site list — one name or several names joined by 'and' both count as provided. A site name is an opaque identifier and may contain digits, underscores and letters that spell RAT terms; that does not stop it from being a site name — never overlook such a name when checking the site list. Only report slot.not_provided when no concrete site name appears, or when the names are introduced as examples or marked incomplete. If the input mentions a power outage but does NOT list specific site names, you MUST report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Site list'. An area name alone is NOT a site list. A count of sites without names (e.g. '10 sites', '5 base stations') means the site list is unspecified — report slot.not_provided (NOT slot.constraint_violated) with slot_label 'Site list'. The value is missing, not invalid. References to sites by area or scope without concrete names (e.g. 'sites in this area', 'all affected sites', 'sites in the region') are NOT a concrete site list — report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Site list'. Site names introduced as examples without a complete list ('sites such as X and Y', 'sites like X', 'e.g. X') MUST report slot.intent_unclear with slot_label 'Site list', even if other errors (e.g. Area violation) are also present. A phrase like 'and a few others' appended to concrete site names indicates the site list is incomplete — the user has not enumerated all affected sites. You MUST report slot.intent_unclear with slot_label 'Site list'. (b) Outage time: must be a concrete clock range (e.g. 'from 08:00 to 12:00'). If the input only gives a relative date (e.g. 'tomorrow') without a clock range, report slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Power outage start/end time'. If a clock range is given with a relative date (e.g. 'from 08:00 to 12:00 tomorrow'), that is acceptable — only the clock range is required, not the date. Outage duration must be a single specific number (e.g. 3 hours), not a range (e.g. '2 or 3 hours'); ranges report slot.intent_unclear with slot_label 'Power outage duration'. A vague duration such as 'more than X hours', 'several hours', 'a few hours', 'some hours' is neither a specific number nor a range — it reports slot.not_provided with slot_label 'Power outage duration', NOT slot.constraint_violated. A vague duration is a missing value, not an invalid one.

expected_output.description: When the task object is a geographic/logical area, output the intent report for the network energy saving task.
expected_output.x-a2at-value-constraint: Basic information about the intent execution result: area, intent goal achievement status. Detailed information about the intent execution result: energy saving gain achievement status (current energy saving gain goal, actual energy saving gain percentage, target adjustment suggestions), rate goal achievement status (current rate goal, actual rate, target adjustment suggestions).
